Construction Considerations
The increased concern for the environment has initiated several pollution control regulations on all phases of roadway and bridge construction.
In addition to the design features in the project plans, the State of Wisconsin Standard Specifications and individual contract special provisions include provisions to preclude degredation of the environment during and after construction. These documents are consistent with the State Department of Matural Pesources Implementation Plan for achieving ambient air quality standards. Contractors are also required to comply with all air pollution control rules and regulations, ordinances and statutes.
Safeguards to protect against the effects of erosion and siltation are as follows:
1. The contractors will be required to submit for approval a plan of operations for accomplishing temporary and continuous erosion control measures for their work.
2. Fording of waterways by construction equipment will be forbidden unless measures which will prevent siltation or damaging channel alteration are employed. Streams in the project area will be restored to a condition which is equal to or better than their original state.
3. The area of erosive land exposed to the elements by grubbing, excavation, horrow and fill operations at any one time will be subject to the approval of the engineer and the duration of such exposure prior to final trimming, finishing and seeding, or application of temporary erosion control measures will be as short as practicable.
4. Grubbing and grading operations will be performed in proper sequence with other work to minimize erosion. Intercepting ditches or dikes will be constructed as soon as practical after clearing and gurbbing operations are completed. Where
